title: Existing-home sales rose 1.5% in September as inventory climbed
dek: NAR counted a 3.99 million annual sales pace, with the median price up 1.3% from a year earlier to $417,500.

body.h: How did home sales do in September 2026?

body.p: Existing-home sales rose 1.5% from August to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.99 million in September 2026, according to the National Association of Realtors report released October 13. Sales were 2.2% lower than in September 2025.
NAR's chief economist, Lawrence Yun, noted that even with the monthly gain, August and September were the two slowest months for sales this year.

body.h: What happened to prices and inventory?

body.p: The national median existing-home price was $417,500, up 1.3% from a year earlier. Inventory rose to 1.60 million homes for sale, equal to a 4.8-month supply at the current sales pace.
First-time buyers made up 31% of sales and all-cash purchases made up 27%, per the same report.

body.h: What about the South, including Texas and Oklahoma?

body.p: NAR does not break out individual states in this release, but its South region, which includes Texas and Oklahoma, posted a 2.8% monthly sales increase to a 1.86 million annual rate. That was down 0.5% from a year earlier. The South's median price was $361,000, up 0.2% year over year.

More inventory and flat prices tilt negotiating power slightly toward buyers. A 4.8-month supply is still below the roughly six months many analysts treat as a balanced market, so sellers are not under heavy pressure yet.

sources.label: National Association of Realtors, existing-home sales release (Oct. 13, 2026)
